item.title: Earth's Increasing Mass
item.description: Lots of SCPs (646, 871, 1680), create a constant stream of mass from nowhere. Is that a problem?
item.content:encoded: I am wondering if the Foundation has any plan for dealing with all the excess mass that results from these SCPs. They've found short-term ways to keep the Keter cakes from overrunning the planet, but the mass of the consumed cakes is still conserved by D-class digestion. The same goes for 646's terminated offspring and 1680's clones of Tyler Buchanan used as D-class. The mass of the SCP-verse's planet Earth is gradually increasing and, without some way to destroy all that mass or send it somewhere else, will continue to do so. Are there other anomalies that are constantly destroying mass and therefore balancing this somewhat? Or is the increase so small that it simply won't matter against the mass of the entire planet?

item.title: A question about the Anomalous Intelligence Community
item.description: Or, "Does the UIU have a rival?"
item.content:encoded:
Not in the sense of groups like the GOC, Foundation and so on and so forth where the Unusual Incidents Unit calling them their 'rivals' would be paying themselves a pretty generous compliment, but instead I mean… well, doing a dive into the UIU hub it occurred to me that the FBI is largely limited in scope to inside of the United States.

Which is all well and good… but, the United States has interests outside of its own borders.

The CIA, conversely, operates mostly abroad as a covert agency.

So, my question is: Does the CIA have its own equivalent to the UIU, or would they borrow a 'specialist' from them in the event they have to deal with something anomalous? Or do they simply hand it off to the Foundation, or the GOC or someone similar?

Has this been addressed in a tale or on one of the hubs?

item.title: Inter-Site Rivalries
item.description: Stereotypes, jokes, etc. that Foundation personnel make about other Foundation facilities.
item.content:encoded:
Looking at the different sorts of objects at different Sites and their varying geographic situations and histories, I wonder what the personnel who’ve never been to other Sites think about them.

For example, ABCA-14 is probably seen as the worst possible assignment (except maybe Site-54) due to its isolated location, 7 different Keters (3 of which have triple digit kill counts), high number of catastrophic breaches, nuclear failsafe, and the presence of Nu-7 making it feel like a military base.

item.title: Trans 'Keter' Clasificaton?
item.description: How does the foundation classify low-threat anomalous objects that simply CAN NOT be "contained", for any appreciable amount of time?
item.content:encoded:
I've been thinking about a number of SCP article ideas about objects that are, unto themselves, extremely low-threat, like a teleporting coin that lands on-edge and stays that way every time it's flipped: but which containment of any sort has proven simply impossible. These objects don't 'breach' containment, they can't even be put into it in the first place. They are known and somewhat studied by the foundation in the field, but just, can't be "Contained"…

Is there an existing classification or sub-classification that is used for this purpose: or does one need to be created?

item.title: Was Duke on Omega-7?
item.description: SCP-083-D's role in Omega-7 and the nuclear destruction of Area-25.
item.content:encoded: SCP-083-D's file says that Area-25 was destroyed by the nuclear failsafe during his ultimate showdown of ultimate destiny with an escaping 076-2, but 076-2's documentation implies that Area-25 was destroyed because Able disabled his explosive collar and went on a rampage because he was bored. 083-D also suggests that he was asked to join Omega-7 after the explosion of Area-25, but 076's files say Omega-7 was disbanded after that. This is contradictory; am I to assume that, since 083-D was decommissioned, its file is "less canon" than the current version of 076's? Where does Duke 'till Dawn fit in, if that's the case? I guess this is related to the Resurrection canon, since that's probably the only canon where both Duke 'till Dawn and Omega-7 canonically happened as described.

item.title: Kondraki Chronology
item.description: When did certain key events in the lives of the Kondraki family take place?
item.content:encoded:
I'm writing a tale that will feature brief cameos by some members of the Kondraki family, and I'm trying to sort out the timeline so I don't create anything too contradictory. Specifically, I'm looking for the dates (or rough estimates) of:

Incident 239-B - Clef-Kondraki
Duke 'till Dawn
Dr. Kondraki's demise in Portraits of Your Father

I'd also like to get a sense of the general timeline of Draven and Researcher Talloran's relationship. From Portraits of Your Father and the …Like Clockwork series I've determined that Dr. Kondraki died when Draven was 25, two years after he started dating Talloran, and that Talloran transferred from Site-17 to Site-118 and battled SCP-3999 in 2017. How long were they and Draven together before then? Any help in ironing (or just vaguely sketching) this out would be appreciated.

item.title: SCP-001 "When Day Breaks" Questions/Theories
item.description: Various questions/theories I have about "When Day Breaks". Feel free to answer them or add more.
item.content:encoded:
SCP-001 "When Day Breaks" is told in the form of a story. But there's something that bothers me. If everyone on Earth was "melted" by the sun, and the main character of the story was dragged into the sun, then how were these events discovered and added to the SCP files? In fact, how was "When Day Breaks" even discovered? Did the Foundation witness these events from a different dimension/universe?

What is the range that the sun's anomalous effects take place? Say if someone was in a distant solar system, would they be affected by our sun's anomalous effects or not?

If I recall correctly, SCP-239 is capable of making her thoughts become reality. The file did say that she can only affect her immediate surroundings, but Dr. Clef stated that she could change reality, so maybe she could be able to revert everything to normal so long as she doesn't come into contact with the sun as it nullifies anomalous effects of beings.

Sorry if everything isn't organized. I'm just spewing out ideas here. Please feel free to answer my questions or to add more questions or theories.

item.title: I need help to understand the themes of the Apotheosis Canon.
item.content:encoded:
Hello Community, would you have some time to talk to me about Apotheosis?

+Introduction
-Close

When the canon was founded, I wanted to know more about what it was all about when it had such an interesting banner and name, but never got around to it. I regularly looked at the Apotheosis hub, but I never took the time to read everything. But when I finished The Exploring the SCP Foundation: Apotheosis 1 / 2 / 3 recently, I wanted to read the guide of this canon right away.


Can someone explain the canon to me?
+Explanation
-Close

Because I really do not understand how I can write for the canon. I know everything that is needed, a big part of humanity gets superpowers, there are many fights and the foundation has a really hard time to get everything under control. It is quite Anime, in a good sense.
I would need a little more information about how the authors imagined the world, except what is written in the articles.
Note: I have also read the entry from The Comprehensive List of K-Class Scenarios.


And is the canon not completed when we know the end?

Thanks for any person who takes the time to patiently write me a reply.

item.title: What is the rank structure of the Foundation?

Hello all! I'm looking to write a few tales drawing inspiration from my irl military experience. Being kind of a paramilitary/governmental organization I was wondering if anyone has yet established a rank structure.
